subject: Interview loop: Senior Serving Engineer — scope, signals & scheduling
messages:
From: GreenLeaf Talent <recruiters@greenleaftalent.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Candidate intro — Sofia Morales (Senior Serving Eng)

Hi Jordan,

Quick intro: we have a strong candidate, Sofia Morales, who is currently at QuantaScale and is exploring next roles focused on inference runtime and serving economics. I attached her resume. She has recent ownership of a production KV cache redesign and led kernel selection work for quantized transformer variants.

Has ~8 years infra/serving experience and is looking for a manager-led loop (1:1 with hiring manager + 3 interviewers). Are you able to confirm scope and who should be on the loop? She is available the week of May 18–22 in the afternoons PT.

Attachments: Sofia_Morales_Resume.pdf (1 page)

Best,
Lindsey Park
GreenLeaf Talent
recruiters@greenleaftalent.com

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: recruiters@greenleaftalent.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Candidate intro — Sofia Morales (Senior Serving Eng)

Thanks Lindsey — forwarding to the hiring loop. Team: brief here on why I want to interview Sofia for the Senior Serving Eng role and how I'd like us to structure the loop so we gather signal we actually need.

Role scope (high level, attach redwood_senior_serving_scope_v2.md):
- Primary: inference serving runtime (continuous batching, KV/prefix caching, kernel selection)
- Secondary: orchestration policies (routing, fallbacks, model variants) and performance SLOs
- Not required: backend web/frontend code — we want deep infra/LLM-serving signal

Leveling expectations (Senior):
- Demonstrates end-to-end ownership of a production-serving subsystem (design + rollout + rollback)
- Can discuss 1–2 concrete kernel/quantization tradeoffs with measurable outcomes
- Leads design with tradeoffs and operational mitigations (e.g., graceful degradation)

Proposed loop & signal per interviewer (please take one each):
- Marissa (hiring manager): 30m, high-level background, ownership examples, leadership judgment
- Markus: 45m system design deep dive — focus on serving runtime architecture + KV cache and kernel selection; expect a whiteboard-style tradeoff conversation
- Laura: 30m performance debugging / telemetry — given a production incident vignette, how would they triage?
- Neha: 20m coding/practical (small performance-focused exercise) + 10m cultural fit / collaboration questions

Rubric (attached interview_rubric_numeric_v1.docx):
- Numeric 1–4 per dimension (1 = insufficient, 4 = exceptional); pass = >=3 in at least 3/4 critical buckets with no 1s in safety-critical areas (production ops, ownership)

Logistics: candidate available May 18–22 afternoons PT. I'd like to offer either May 20 13:00 PT or May 22 11:00 PT as options. Please confirm your availability for those slots and whether you want the quantization deep-dive included in Markus's design slot.

Attachments: redwood_senior_serving_scope_v2.md; interview_rubric_numeric_v1.docx

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior PM, Hiring (Acting) — Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, recruiters@greenleaftalent.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Candidate intro — Sofia Morales (Senior Serving Eng)

Jordan — good plan. Quick clarifying Qs:
1) Quantization deep-dive — do we expect device-level quantization math or higher-level tradeoffs? I prefer focusing on measurable perf/accuracy tradeoffs and a single concrete example (e.g., 8-bit kernel choice) rather than low-level math.
2) Incident vignette for Laura — do we want to use the 2025 cache-regression incident doc as the canonical artifact? If so I can prep a shortened timeline + logs for a 30m triage.

If everyone is OK, I'll take the design slot and include a short kernel-selection prompt that asks for comparative metrics and rollback strategy. Availability: May 20 13:00 PT works for me.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Staff Serving Eng — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, recruiters@greenleaftalent.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Candidate intro — Sofia Morales (Senior Serving Eng)

Thanks Jordan — small adjustments from the hiring manager POV:
- Reduce coding to 20m and make it strongly performance-oriented (micro-optimizations, explaining tradeoffs). The goal is signal on system-level thinking, not algorithmic puzzles.
- Add a short "rollout story" prompt to my slot: candidate should walk a recent rollout that had a perf regression and explain mitigations.
- For rubric: can we add a hard check that the candidate has shipped a kernel/optimization that moved the needle (if not, it's a weak signal)? This is a tiebreaker for staff-level consideration.

Scheduling: I prefer May 20 13:00 PT. Laura — can you take the telemetry triage? Neha — can you take the coding slot (20m) plus 10m culture? I've included Lindsey (recruiter) in Cc so we can lock candidate availability.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Hiring Manager, Inference Serving — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Sofia Morales <sofia.morales@gmail.com>

Hi Marissa / Jordan,

Thanks for the details and the suggested slots. I can confirm May 20 at 1:00 PM PT works well for me. I appreciate the heads-up on focus areas — I will prepare a rollout story and a kernel-selection example from QuantaScale.

Attached: Sofia_Morales_Resume.pdf (updated header with Phone). Happy to share a brief code sample if it helps for the coding slot.
